commitments.text: 1. Lafarge shall cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed, operated, dismantled, and abandoned in accordance with the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate, collectively comprising the proponent's application, and without limiting the generality of the forgoing, Lafarge must fulfil all commitments and proposed mitigation measures as documented in the application.

3. Despite Condition 1 above, Lafarge may request of authorities required to give approvals, licenses, permits or other authorisations under other enactments for implementation of the Project, variation of the Project design, location, construction, operation, dismantling and abandonment outlined in the documents in Schedule A to this Certificate, in accordance with that authority's approval process, provided that the variation is not a project modification which constitutes a reviewable project under the provisions of the Environmental Assessment Reviewable Projects Regulation (BC Reg. 276/95).
4. Lafarge must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, have substantially started the Project within five years of the issue date of this Certificate.

7. Lafarge must comply with all applicable orders, directions and conditions, and obtain and comply with all applicable tenures, licences, regulations, approvals, standards and permits, or other authorities, which may include or result from, but are not necessarily limited to, the following enactments: a) Commercial Transport Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 55; b) Fisheries Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 137; c) Fire Services Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c.133; d) Health Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 161; e) Heritage Conservation Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 165; f) Highway Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 167; g) Motor Vehicle Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 288; h) Power Engineers A Boiler K Pressure Vessel Safety Act, S.B.C. 1981, c. 25; i) Transport of Dangerous Goods Act, S.B.C. 1985, c. 17; j) Waste Management Act, S.B.C. 1982, c. 41; k) Water Act, R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 429.

8. Lafarge shall hire a qualified archaeologist to monitor construction of the Project, comply with permits issued under section 7 of the Heritage Conservation Act, and report the results of the monitoring to the person responsible for the Archaeology Branch, Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture.

9. Lafarge shall: a) prepare, in consultation with the Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, the Greater Vancouver Regional District, and the Ministry of Employment and Investment, a Greenhouse Gases Mitigation Plan including details of proposed offsets for greenhouse gas emissions. This plan is to be subnitted, by December 31, 1996, to the person responsible for the Air Quality Department, Greater Vancouver Regional District, the person responsible for the Air Resources Branch, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, and the person responsible for the Policy Division, Ministry of Employment and Investment, for review and approval. Lafarge will implement those portions of the plan that are, in the reasonable opinion of the above-named persons and after consultation with experts supplied by Lafarge, technically and economically feasible.

9. Lafarge shall: b) prepare, in consultation with the Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, the Greater Vancouver Regional District, the City of Richmond and the Fraser River Harbour Commission, an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) that addresses monitoring and control of construction impacts, and monitoring and control of impacts once the Project is operating, including a plan for emergency response and materials handling; submit the EMP to representatives of the above-named agencies before construction of the Project; implement the EMP to the reasonable satisfaction of representatives of the above-named agencies, and report to them at regular intervals as required.
